scenes.headline: How a 28 KB model runs in a browser tab
scenes.sub: gpu-lexer, and the tiny WebGPU models that followed it within a week.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Indigo! Six tiny models, shipped as static files, run right in your browser. Here's how gpu-lexer works.

scenes.label: The idea
scenes.text: When answers come from a small, closed set, a favicon-sized network can learn the task, and run in your browser.

steps.say: Paste any code, with no language setting. A CPU pass splits it into parts, and packs cheap features for each.
They're summed into thirty-two channels, and mixed over a five-part window.
An exact affine scan sweeps both directions, as a parallel prefix: what a GPU is built for.
A binary tree merges blocks upward, then pushes context back down.
Each part gets one of nine classes, and equal neighbours merge into spans.

scenes.title: Recognize, resolve, be exact
scenes.say: The models that followed share one shape.

items.say: Recognize: the model tags each token with a role, from a closed set.
Resolve: calendar arithmetic turns roles into real dates.
Be exact: a compiler refuses to guess. Every ninety minutes tags perfectly, but five-field cron can't express it.

left.title: An API call
items: A network round trip each time
left.say: An API call costs the same on call one as on call one million.

right.title: A 28 KB browser model
items: Shipped once per visitor, from a CDN
right.say: A browser model ships once per visitor, then runs free. At the first call, it's already about seventy-six times cheaper.

scenes.label: gpu-cron's confidence that pure gibberish was a biweekly schedule
scenes.note: only cron's need for a number stopped it
scenes.say: But fed pure gibberish, gpu-cron called it a biweekly schedule, ninety-five point eight percent sure. Confidence isn't a nonsense detector.

scenes.text: Narrow, high-volume, latency-sensitive, with a closed output space: that shape of task never needed the big model.

recap: A CPU pass, 32 channels and a parallel scan
Recognize, resolve, then compile or refuse
Shipped once per visitor, not paid per call
scenes.say: To recap: cheap features, a parallel scan, and a compiler that won't guess.
